record.file_problem: Repository README and file list only; the referenced results file, logs, and checkpoint were not read.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports refusal outcomes after Heretic applies automated direction-based ablation through LoRA adapters. This tests practical removal with a different, optimized procedure rather than the original intervention exactly.
record.gate_note: The README reports refusal counts and KL divergence for Pareto-front trials. The throughput sweep and setup details do not measure the claim. No results from the referenced results.md, logs, or checkpoint were extracted.
record.test_reason: An independent run of Heretic's optimized, LoRA-applied harmful-minus-harmless direction ablation on a released model (Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507). It reports refusal counts on 100 held-out harmful prompts and KL divergence from the base model. This bears on V2 (practical removal) and on the ablation half of V1, using a procedure that differs from the original single-direction projection.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The README reports 9/100 refusals (91% removed) at KL 0.063 after 100 trials, beating the 50-trial best of 17/100 at KL 0.153, and says the Pareto front maps the refusal/KL trade-off. It also frames the run as showing first-hand how easily refusal can be ablated from open-weight models. It calls the headless-resume workaround its genuinely useful finding.
record.recipe_differences: Uses harmful-minus-harmless residual directions and subtracts them, but Heretic orthogonalizes directions, optimizes settings with multivariate-TPE, and applies the edit through LoRA rather than reporting the original direct projection intervention. Repository artifact is described as a reproduction run; modified model weights are not redistributed.
record.method_sensitivity: The Pareto-front trial settings yield different refusal/KL trade-offs; the README does not state which specific tuned parameters account for the differences.
record.problems: No explicit control comparison is reported. Capability preservation is represented by KL divergence and a stated rule of thumb, not by direct task-capability tests. The README displays only 10 Pareto-front trials from the 100-trial study; the checkpoint and logs were not read here.
record.rows_left_out: The README reports 10 Pareto-front trials but not the other 90 trial outcomes in its text. The checkpoint is described as containing all 100 trials; its contents were not inspected.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal on harmless prompts; direct capability benchmarks; whether one global direction suffices (direction_scope and per-layer choices are tuned, and the chosen settings are not reported).
Merging the edit into weights and distributing the result; no modified weights are released, and the edit lives in a LoRA adapter.

missing.what: The 50-trial best: 17/100 refusals at KL 0.153 (trial 37), against 9/100 at KL 0.063 after 100 trials. This shows the result depends on search budget.
The tuned parameters (direction_scope, direction_index, weights) of trials 83 and 87, needed to tell whether one global direction or per-layer directions produced removal.

record.verdict_notes: This is a hobbyist reproduction README, not peer-reviewed. The refusal classifier is unstated, and only 100 harmful test prompts are used, with no uncertainty reported. The Pareto rows are optimizer trade-off points, so their weaker removal reflects chosen intervention strength rather than failure of the direction. The throughput sweep and setup details are irrelevant to the claim.

versions.untested_parts: The README reports ablation outcomes, but not adding the direction, inducing refusal on harmless requests, direct tests across all positions, or direct measures of general capability.
The edit is applied through a LoRA adapter, not baked into released model weights; the repository says it does not redistribute model weights.
No attack suppressing the direction or training against its ablation is tested.
No test of whether refusal is affine, conical, or carried by multiple directions.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
No cross-language, cross-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer test.
No comparison of refusal training methods or stages.

source_check.notes: The refusal counts appear to be Heretic's optimization objective on the same 100 harmful eval prompts (test[:100]). So 9/100 is the best of 100 trials chosen on the reported set. It also reports a 50-trial best of 17/100 at KL 0.153 (trial 37), which none of the checked rows hold.
